- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent 10-day mean), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent peak within 5 days), model often fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–7 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days to catch momentum.
